cost: THE ROUND IS A CONFLICT BETWEEN TWO OF HIS OWN RULINGS AND IT IS RESOLVED IN THE SUBJECT'S FAVOUR — HE SHOULD KNOW THAT. CLINT CAPELA '18 is pinned off 61 +-1 by recal_52, read 62, and now reads 60: he keeps his pin but lands on its FLOOR instead of its ceiling, a two-point fall, and he loses recal_112's term entirely. He is not collateral, he is the SAME CARD as the subject at everything this term reads — true shooting relative to the league .664 against .660, usage 19.3 against 19.3, and a HIGHER efficiency rating (91 against 88), so his gate before the round (0.143) was already ABOVE the subject's (0.121). The only quantity that separates them is volume, 45 against 38. That is why the band's top had to come below 45, and it is why the two constants are FORCED rather than chosen: with his pin held, any linear volume factor that reaches the subject must have its top at or below ~47 and its foot at or above ~35. If he would rather Capela '18 stayed at 62, this round cannot land at all — measured, not asserted: of 720 parameterisations of this gate's whole family, exactly ONE holds every anchor with the subject unmoved, and it is the shipped one.

THE FRONTIER, MEASURED. 720 parameterisations of the gate (efficiency foot 82/85, top 86 to 99; volume foot 25/35, top 45 to 70; size 0.14 and 0.20; product, geometric mean and fourth root), each graded against every standing anchor: 83 hold the whole board and the highest reading any of them gives the subject is 69. The setting taken reaches his band at the SMALLEST worst-case move: 65 with a max of +7. The settings that read 66, 67 and 68 all take the board's worst move to +9 or +10, and he declined recal_132 for two cards rising 10+.

COLLATERAL IS 152 CARDS ON OFF, 138 up and 14 down, mean +3.78, max +7 and max -3. NOTHING MOVES BY 8 OR MORE. The 14 that fall are the cards between volume 45 and 55 that the band's top no longer reaches, and the largest of them is Clint Capela '18 at -3 raw (-2 printed). DEF moves on ZERO cards and every attribute on ZERO. OVR follows on 134, max +5 and max -2. The top 12 by OFF is identical name for name and the top 50 by OVR has no entrant and no leaver.

THE MOVERS ARE ONE ARCHETYPE AND READ LIKE IT: the efficient low-usage interior man recal_112 was built for and was paying an eighth of what it claimed — Jarrett Allen '22-'25, Rudy Gobert '17/'18, Artis Gilmore '81-'84, Otis Thorpe '91/'92, Buck Williams '82/'83, Danny Schayes '88/'89, Darryl Dawkins '83, Nic Claxton '23, Jalen Duren '25, Neemias Queta '26, Tyson Chandler '11/'12, Dikembe Mutombo '00.

WHAT IS NOT FIXED, and a later ruling would have to name it. The subject lands at 65 against 66 +-2, one below his number, and the reason is the same pin: every setting that reads him at 66 or above takes some card on the board up by 9 or more. His own '10 still reads 5 above him (70 to 65) and that gap is now made of things the formula should price — ts_rel .668 against .660 at usage 17.3 against 19.3 — rather than of a product compounding two small slides.

THE THREE OTHER CHANNELS WERE MEASURED AND NONE OF THEM REACHES THIS CARD. recal_131's paint-evidence floor is gated volume 55->80 and he is 38, and even at a full gate his evidence beats his zone block by only 1.1 raw. recal_37's PAINT DOMINANCE BONUS does fire on his shape (rim 73 against mid 28 and 3pt 7, so z[0] > 1.5 x the rest) but recal_51's volume ramp zeroes his attempt factor below volume 70 and recal_44's free-throw gate would clamp him to 0.25 anyway — his 71 FT stroke is what the standard path already pays him for. Opening either would pay Clint Capela '18 MORE than the subject, not less, because Capela's rim bar is 89 to the subject's 73 and his FT stroke is 57 to the subject's 71.

HUNT and CRASH DEF GLASS both broke on the BLIND edge together (-0.2993 and -0.2788 against the -0.30 ceiling) because the round pushed another block of bigs across the harness's `ovr >= 55` pool line, so the fives are stronger and a blind call costs less against them. hunt swept 3.80 (-0.2993) / 3.808 (-0.3054) / 3.85 (-0.3380) / 3.95 (oracle +0.515) / 3.98 (+0.5005) / 3.99 (+0.4957, under) — feasible about 3.801 to 3.981, midpoint 3.89. crashDef swept .48 (-0.2788) / .502 (-0.2943) / .53 (-0.3141) / .67 (+0.549, blind -0.414) / .80 (+0.509) / .829 (+0.5001) / .831 (under) — feasible about .510 to .830, midpoint .67. Both take their true midpoints by recal_126's rule: hunt 3.80 -> 3.89, crashDef .48 -> .67. crashOff held at .17, playmaker at 1.10, and the six other bands were untouched. All nine pass.

THE FULL CHAIN WAS NOT RUN. build_ratings.py was not run and provenance.json is unchanged: this round is compute_ovr.py only, plus the two tax constants the harness law requires be re-read whenever the ovr>=55 pool moves.
notes: THE DEFECT IN ONE SENTENCE: recal_112's gate is the PRODUCT of two ramps that are two readings of ONE claim — 'his conversion is elite FOR his usage' — so a card that slides a little on both loses far more than either slide justifies, and one of the two ramps saturated at the top of the scale, where eleven cards live.

THE SUBJECT DECOMPOSED. Nenê '11 reads 60 and his own '10 reads 70, and the whole ten points is this one term: '10 takes it at gate 1.00 (+13.86) and '11 at 0.12 (+1.50). Efficiency 99 -> 88 and volume 25 -> 38 are both real and both modest; 0.21 x 0.57 = 0.12 is not. Nothing else on the two sheets moves — rim 72/73, orb 67/65, free throws identical, playvol 33/38.

IT IS recal_117's ITEM 4, ONE TERM DOWN THE FILE. Its words: 'Volume was read TWICE ... and the product of two decreasing factors is steeper than either.' Its rule was READ THE FACT ONCE. Here the two factors are different facts but one claim, so the fix is the same in kind: the geometric mean is the single share whose square is the product.

THE GEOMETRIC MEAN CHANGES NO EXCLUSION, and that is verified rather than assumed. It is zero whenever either share is zero, so the efficiency foot of 85 still excludes Deandre Ayton '26 (81), Clint Capela '17 (79) and Domantas Sabonis '21 (70); the playvol ceiling of 70 still excludes John Stockton '96 (99) and keeps this term disjoint from recal_109's elite passer; and the 3pt ceiling of 68 still excludes Kyle Korver '15 (95) and Steve Kerr '96 (93) and keeps it disjoint from recal_64's off-ball floor. All five move by exactly zero.

THE NEEDLE, MEASURED THE WAY recal_117 MEASURED ITS OWN. Inside this term's class — 4,256 cards at 3pt < 68, playvol < 70, volume < 55 — efficiency 85 is the top 4.42% (188 cards) and efficiency 99 is the top 0.26% (ELEVEN cards). Only SIX cards on the whole board had a gate of 1.00, and the median gate among the 172 with any gate at all was 0.256. The re-cut top, 93, is the measured UPPER QUARTILE of the 188 that clear the foot.

CLINT CAPELA '19 IS THE PROOF THIS IS A RULE AND NOT A NAME CHECK. The same man one season later — efficiency 90, volume 37 — rises 59 -> 65 on the very rule that takes his '18 from 62 to 60, because '18 is volume 45 and '19 is volume 37. The band reads usage, not names.
